state.product: MenteViva, iOS cognitive-exercise app. Warm, no-fail, big-target design. One binary, per-person libraries: an older family member gets familiarity-based games; mom/owner (healthy 60s/40s) get speed/logic/attention games. Copy ceiling: 'fun mental exercise', no medical claims. Zero third-party deps, solo developer.
state.players: Primary: an older family member who needs errorless familiarity-based play. Secondary: mom/owner, healthy adults who want engaging challenge and buy/gift the app.
state.evidence: Meta-analysis CCT effect small (g~0.22, 51 studies); MCI/early dementia best-supported population; processing speed strongest-evidence domain; spaced retrieval and errorless learning supported for memory-impaired; numeracy weakest domain; no dementia prevention claims allowed.
state.playtest_findings: Informal family playtest: scoring confusing and meaningless; games get boring; visuals not attractive enough.
state.prior_judgment: Jev 008 (dad only): Memory Lane 1.76 core-leaning, Name the Herd 1.27 unsure, Color Clash 0.24, Number Trail 0.12, Quick Eyes 0.01 deprioritized for dad; reminiscence next game 0.92. This matrix re-scores for the whole household and adds cost-to-polish.

games.memory_lane: emoji pair matching, working/episodic memory, already dad-suitable
games.color_clash: Stroop color-word inhibition, error-inducing by design
games.name_the_herd: tap items belonging to a category, verbal fluency
games.quick_eyes: shrinking display-time visual discrimination, processing speed
games.reminiscence_candidate: NOT YET BUILT: recognize/name familiar objects and family-provided photos; reminiscence + familiarity; highest evidence fit for dad per Jev 008
